items.title: Home Secretary unveils new rules for migrants settling in the UK
items.body: The Home Secretary has set out new rules for migrants settling in the UK. Under the changes, settlement will be earned through contribution and good character.

items.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
items.body: Britain and the EU have reached a significant food trade deal ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month, removing customs barriers on food exports. The agreement is the most substantial part of the so-called Brexit reset achieved to date.

items.title: UK job satisfaction drops to record low amid pay and flexibility concerns
items.body: A study by the Resolution Foundation shows job satisfaction among British workers has hit an all-time low, driven by frustration over pay, insecure contracts and lack of flexible working. Workers are also less willing to go above and beyond for employers than a decade ago.

items.title: AI-powered cyber attacks on UK infrastructure expected by 2028
items.body: The National Cyber Security Centre warns that artificial intelligence is "helping to industrialise cyber attacks" and is highly likely to be used against Britain's critical infrastructure including power stations, airports and hospitals within two years.

items.title: UK MPs could face criminal record checks to prevent violence against women
items.body: Parliament is set to become the first legislature to require MPs and staff to undergo criminal record checks before receiving security passes and receive anti-harassment training. The measure aims to tackle violence against women in the workplace.

items.title: British Gas resumes force-fitting prepay meters despite record settlement
items.body: British Gas has resumed installing prepay meters in homes of customers who cannot afford energy bills, months after paying the largest regulatory settlement on record for sending debt collectors to vulnerable households. Regulator Ofgem has lifted the block.

items.title: Major study launched to measure "forever chemicals" in UK population
items.body: The government is launching the first study to measure PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) in the UK population to understand health risks. Forever chemicals are persistent pollutants found in many consumer products and the environment.

items.title: Horse sold by King Charles wins Melbourne Cup
items.body: Point of Law, a horse previously sold by King Charles, has won Australia's Melbourne Cup, ridden by Ethan Brown. The race is known as the "race that stops a nation".
